The church clarified this in a post on its official X account on Friday, urging members and the public to disregard reports that worship activities had been stopped. “Don’t believe the noise; church is not sealed, see you in church on Sunday,” the church stated. In a separate message, it invited worshippers to attend its 9am service, either physically or online. “Don’t believe the noise! Join us for service every Sunday at TFOLC. There’s a place for you; you can join us in person or online! 9AM WAT. We look forward to welcoming you!” the message read. The announcement comes amid a leadership dispute that has resulted in legal proceedings over who should lead the church. On Wednesday, November 18, the Lagos State High Court restrained Odukoya from presenting himself as the Senior Pastor and Spiritual Head of the church following an application by the Incorporated Trustees of The Fountain of Life Church. Justice O.O. Adewunmi-Oshin also barred him, whether acting personally or through proxies, from interfering with, disrupting or obstructing the church’s activities, governance and other business. However, the court order did not direct the closure or sealing of the church premises. The interim orders were granted ex parte, meaning Odukoya’s response was not heard before they were made. He retains the right to challenge the orders and respond to the substantive claims. The matter was adjourned until December 1, 2026, for mention. The leadership crisis became public on November 17 when a faction of the church’s Board of Trustees announced that it had withdrawn recognition of Odukoya as Senior Pastor, citing a December 2021 video in which the late founder, Pastor Taiwo Odukoya, reportedly outlined his preferred succession arrangement. The trustees subsequently named Pastor Rotimi Okpaise as interim spiritual and administrative leader. Jimmy Odukoya and the church leadership, however, rejected the decision, insisting that his appointment as Senior Pastor in September 2023 was valid. Meanwhile, the church had separately announced the postponement of its 2026 Thanksgiving Service, which was scheduled for Sunday, November 22, saying a new date would be communicated. The latest announcement confirms that the regular Sunday worship service will hold, despite the postponement of the Thanksgiving programme and the unresolved leadership dispute.
